newsitem.title: USA: Carnival rises on First Boston comments.
newsitem.headline: Carnival rises on First Boston comments.

text.p: Shares of cruise operator Carnival Corp rose on Tuesday after CS First Boston initiated coverage of the stock with a buy rating and a 12-month price target of $55 a share.
First Boston, in a research brief by analyst David Anders, said that the Florida-based company is rapidly becoming a leading global leisure company.
Shares of Carnival rose 1-2/16 to 43-13/16 in afternoon trade.
Already a major player in the U.S., Carnival has said it plans to start cruising in Asia in 1998. And Anders said that there are "significant" opportunities for growth in Europe.

He noted that favorable demographics and an otherwise favorable economic backdrop will drive demand for cruises and leisure services, and that Carnival will benefit from that demand growth. He said Carnival will continue to acquire and develop other types of leisure activity business. That strategy builds upon Carnival's 1996 purchase of a 30 pct stake in British holirator Airtours Plc.
He estimated the company's annual earnings per share growth at 15 to 20 percent, with 1997 EPS seen at $2.20 a share, 1998 EPS at $2.53 and 1999 EPS at $2.97 per share.
